knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0
knowledge_weighting.note: top_knowledge/top_skills are the unweighted mean over all linked occupations (kept for comparison); the outline uses the entry-weighted lists.

skipped_knowledge.reason: management and planning knowledge matters most after several years of experience, so the outline gives it no course slot (a management elective is optional)
office procedures and records handling; usually learned on the job, so it gets no course slot
teaching and training others is built through presenting, tutoring and peer teaching in projects rather than a dedicated course

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 3 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other titles; no other linked title survives the stricter filter, so first-line supervisor and director titles were allowed), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first; no eligible Job Zone 4 occupation is linked to this major, so Job Zone 3 was used

entry_target_review.note: Kept with a caveat: the crosswalk links only supervisor, faculty and residual codes to this CIP, so the Job Zone 3 correctional-supervisor title is the closest available target. Supervisor roles normally require prior line experience; line-officer occupations are not linked to this CIP in the crosswalk.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role (supervisor roles normally require prior line experience). You supervise the evening shift in a 400-bed county jail. Write the procedure for a scheduled formal count: how officers count, how counts are reported and reconciled with the population record, the time limits, what happens if the count does not clear (recount, lockdown, notifications), and how the count and any discrepancy are documented.

rubric.description: Count method ensures each person is physically observed and reconciled with records.
Clear escalation for a count that does not clear, including recount and notifications.
Records times, officers, numbers, discrepancies and resolution.

reference_answer_outline: All movement stops; officers count by sight, verifying living, breathing persons.
Housing units report to central control; reconcile with roster including court, medical and work assignments.
Recount within set minutes; if still off, lockdown and name check.
Notify the shift commander and follow escape or emergency procedures.
Count sheets signed and retained.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role. Your department adopted an updated body-worn camera policy: cameras must be activated at the start of every enforcement contact, officers may not review footage before writing a use-of-force report until after an initial statement, and certain sensitive locations require notification. Prepare a 10-minute roll-call briefing: key changes, why they matter, three realistic scenarios to discuss, likely questions with answers, and how you will check that officers understand and follow the policy.

rubric.description: States changes accurately and explains reasons such as transparency and evidence integrity.
Scenarios are realistic and promote discussion of judgment calls.
Includes follow-up such as footage audits and coaching.

reference_answer_outline: What changed and effective date.
Reasons: public trust, evidence quality, legal requirements.
Scenarios: traffic stop that escalates, medical call, interview in a hospital.
Answers to questions on privacy and malfunctions.
Monthly random footage audits and individual feedback.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role. You supervise 12 officers on a night shift with two officers out sick, a housing unit with recent fights, and a medical transport scheduled at 03:00. Write the shift plan: post assignments and minimum staffing, briefing priorities, how you supervise rounds and security checks, response plans for a fight or medical emergency, and how you ensure humane treatment and documentation throughout the shift.

rubric.description: Assigns posts to cover critical areas and handles shortages within policy.
Defines checks on rounds, communication and incident response.
Includes humane treatment, medical access and full documentation.

reference_answer_outline: Post chart; overtime or reassignments to cover minimums.
Briefing: tension in the unit, transport details, officer safety.
Supervisor tours and verification of round logs.
Emergency response roles; medical escort procedures.
Shift log entries and incident reports before end of shift.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role. A resident files a complaint that an officer was rude and refused to give his badge number during a traffic stop; footage exists. Write the investigation plan: intake and classification of the complaint, notice to the officer and rights under policy and any labor agreement, evidence to gather (footage, dispatch records, witness statements), interview approach, the standard of proof and possible findings, and how the complainant is informed of the outcome.

rubric.description: Follows policy and due-process protections for the officer and treats the complainant respectfully.
Collects and weighs objective evidence before interviews and conclusions.
Uses defined findings categories and communicates the outcome appropriately.

reference_answer_outline: Log and classify as a courtesy complaint; assign investigator.
Notify officer per contract; preserve footage.
Gather footage, CAD records, witness information.
Interviews: complainant first, then officer; record statements.
Findings: sustained, not sustained, exonerated, unfounded; letter to complainant.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role. After visitor complaints about disrespectful treatment at a jail's visiting area, you are asked to improve officers' professional conduct. Write the monitoring and feedback plan: observable behaviors you will look for, how you observe (walkthroughs, camera review, visitor feedback), how you give feedback and coaching, recognition for good conduct, and when you escalate to formal discipline.

rubric.description: Professional conduct is described in observable terms.
Uses direct observation, video and feedback sources fairly.
Balances coaching and recognition with consistent escalation.

reference_answer_outline: Behaviors: greeting, clear explanations of rules, calm tone, no sarcasm.
Weekly walkthroughs, random video review, visitor comment cards.
Same-day private feedback; coaching plans.
Recognition in briefings and evaluations.
Repeated or serious incidents referred under the discipline policy.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Practice for a later supervisory role. Your squad's incident reports are often late or incomplete, and a recent court case was harmed by a missing evidence log entry. Write a records plan for your squad: report quality standards, review and approval timelines, evidence and chain-of-custody logging, storage and retention requirements, public records requests, and how you train officers and track compliance.

rubric.description: Defines what complete, accurate reports must include.
Addresses evidence logging, secure storage and retention rules.
Includes training and measurable tracking such as on-time report rate.

reference_answer_outline: Report standards: who, what, when, where, how, narrative clarity.
Supervisor review within one shift; returned reports corrected within 24 hours.
Evidence logged at intake with continuous custody records.
Retention schedule; public records requests routed to records unit.
Weekly metrics and refresher training.
